channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Repsol to challenge €20.5 million margin squeeze fine in Spain
item.description: One of Spain's leading fuel suppliers will appeal against a €20.5 million fine by the country’s antitrust watchdog for squeezing the margins of low-cost service stations when Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.

item.title: CMA criticises tribunal’s by object assessment in standalone RPM ruling
item.description: The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority has told an appellate court that the country’s specialist antitrust tribunal “fell into error” when ruling that a major footwear supplier’s online sales policy amounted to a by object infringement.

item.title: X-factor: The Tipline for 3 February 2026
item.description: Elon Musk has further consolidated his business empire by having SpaceX acquire xAI. The formation of the $1.2 trillion company on Monday follows xAI’s acquisition of the social network X last year. Musk said the company would be “one of the most ambitious, vertically integrated innovation engines on (and off) Earth”. item.title: GOP challenge Netflix on YouTube rivalry claim
item.description: Republicans on the Senate Antitrust Subcommittee have rejected claims from the Netflix chief executive that YouTube is a primary competitor.

item.title: Kirkland, Covington steer closing of complex Disney/NFL deal
item.description: The Department of Justice has permitted Disney to acquire NFL Media in exchange for a 10% equity stake in ESPN.

item.title: The whole nine yards: The Briefing for 4 February 2026
item.description: Google is once again facing scrutiny in Turkey, after the country’s antitrust enforcer announced what appears to be its ninth probe into the tech company. The agency said today it will scrutinise contractual agreements with phone makers that provide “financial incentives” to exclusively place the Google Search widget on home screens. item.title: Van Bael & Bellis rebuilds in London
item.description: Van Bael & Bellis has hired Becket McGrath to steer its UK competition practice after losing its former antitrust head in London to Pinsent Masons.

item.title: Firms challenge serial acquisitions safeguards in New Zealand competition overhaul
item.description: Proposals to expand the New Zealand Commerce Commission’s oversight of serial acquisitions in merger reviews are “excessively broad” and may “deter” legitimate investments into the country, leading law firms have said in response to a wide-ranging government consultation.

item.title: FTC settles Section 5 suit with Express Scripts
item.description: Express Scripts has agreed to stop giving preferential treatment to more expensive drugs to resolve the Federal Trade Commission’s claims that the Cigna subsidiary and other pharmacy benefit managers unfairly inflated prices.

item.description: Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson is taking on a second job.
